steam.infoText: Steam presents the DualSense to the game as a standard Xbox controller and forwards the game's rumble to it. Game files are not touched; no extra drivers or admin rights are needed.
steam.step1: Add Rocket League to Steam as a 'non-Steam game' (for the Epic version)
steam.step1Detail: Steam → Games → Add a Non-Steam Game → Browse → select the file below → Add Selected Programs. If the game does not start because of EAC, add Launcher.exe from the same folder. Keep the Epic Games Launcher running in the background.
steam.step2: Enable Steam Input for the game
steam.step2Detail: In the Steam library: Rocket League → right-click → Properties → Controller → 'Enable Steam Input'.
steam.step3Detail: Steam → Settings → Controller → 'PlayStation Controller Support'. Make sure rumble is not disabled in the controller settings.
steam.step4Detail: Pick the 'Gamepad' template in the in-game controller layout. The game now sees the DualSense as an Xbox controller and rumble goes to the controller through Steam.
steam.footnote: Conflicts: if bridges such as DS4Windows, DSX or reWASD, or this app's Mode 2 bridge, are running, the controller shows up twice. Close them while using Mode 1. If HidHide cloaking is on, Steam cannot see the controller.

bridge.intro: The DualSense is read directly over HID (USB or Bluetooth), passed to a virtual Xbox 360 controller (ViGEmBus), and the game's rumble (large motor = left, small motor = right) is written back to the DualSense. When stopped, the motors are zeroed and the virtual controller is removed.
bridge.hidhide: HidHide (optional) · hides the real controller from the game, prevents double input
bridge.footnote: Motor strength, swap and lightbar settings are on the Settings page. If the bridge closes during a match, the virtual controller disappears and the game loses it; minimize to the tray instead of closing. If Steam is open, turn off PlayStation support in Steam so it does not grab the controller too.

proxy.eacText: Rocket League is protected by Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC). Putting a foreign DLL in the game folder can stop the game from starting, trigger EAC errors or get your account penalized. Not recommended for online play. 'Uninstall' restores the original state.
proxy.accept: I understand and accept the risk
proxy.acceptDetail: I want to put a DLL in the Rocket League folder. Install/Uninstall stay disabled until this is on.
proxy.intro: An embedded x64 XInput DLL (written in C) is copied to the game folder. When the game loads XInput, this DLL reads the DualSense directly over HID, presents it as player 1 and writes XInputSetState rumble to the DualSense. Without a DualSense it forwards calls to the original (backed-up) DLL or to System32 XInput.
proxy.installTip: Puts the DLL in the game folder and backs up the original
proxy.uninstallTip: Deletes the proxy and restores the original DLL
proxy.notesText:
• The app does not ask for admin rights. If the game folder is protected, UAC is asked once, only during Install/Uninstall.
• The original DLL is backed up as '<name>_original.dll' and a record file (DualSenseRumbleHelper.proxy.json) is written; Uninstall reverts both. If Epic 'Verify' runs, the file goes back to the original anyway and Uninstall cleans up the extra backup.
• If HidHide cloaking is on, whitelist RocketLeague.exe in HidHide; otherwise the proxy DLL cannot see the controller.
• The game may also see the real DualSense through DirectInput (double input). There is no safe way to prevent this in this mode.
• The motor settings on the Settings page do not apply to this mode (the DLL runs inside the game).
